speaker: Doctor
text:
The presence of smudge cells on the peripheral smear, combined with your age, splenomegaly, and lymphocytosis, strongly points to Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL). Let me examine your neck and armpits to check for swollen lymph nodes, which is common in this condition.

REQUEST TEST: Flow_Cytometry

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal flow cytometry results contradict the initial suspicion of CLL, so I must consider alternative diagnoses like prolymphocytic leukemia or other lymphoproliferative disorders. Do you have any history of recurrent infections or noticeable swelling in your lymph nodes? REQUEST TEST: Bone_Marrow_Biopsy

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the bone marrow biopsy is normal and flow cytometry was negative, I must reconsider the differential diagnosis beyond typical CLL. Given the splenomegaly and lymphocytosis with smudge cells, could you describe any history of autoimmune conditions or recurrent infections? REQUEST TEST: Immunoglobulin_Levels

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal immunoglobulins, bone marrow, and flow cytometry, I must reconsider if the smudge cells were artifactual or if this represents a different lymphoproliferative disorder like Hairy Cell Leukemia. Do you have any history of dental infections or skin nodules, and are you experiencing any abdominal pain due to the enlarged spleen? REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_CT_Scan

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal abdominal CT scan rules out significant lymphadenopathy or organ infiltration, which makes typical lymphoproliferative disorders like Hairy Cell Leukemia or CLL less likely despite the smudge cells. Since the imaging and marrow are normal, I need to rule out a reactive process or a rare entity like Splenic Marginal Zone Lymphoma that might not show up on standard CT. Do you have any history of chronic liver disease, such as cirrhosis, or have you noticed any skin rashes or joint pain recently? REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Tests
